newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April-Sept trade surplus plunges 41 percent.
newsitem.headline: Japan April-Sept trade surplus plunges 41 percent.

text.p: Japan's closely watched trade surplus fell more than 41 percent in the six months from April to September from the same period a year earlier, confirming that the controversial surplus is still on a shrinking trend, government data showed on Friday.

The Ministry of Finance said the unadjusted customs-cleared trade surplus fell to 2.90 trillion yen ($25.8 billion at the current rate of around 112 yen to the dollar) in the period, the first half of Japan's fiscal year.
Meanwhile, the trade surplus with the United States in the six-month period fell 24.2 percent from the previous year to 1.56 trillion yen ($13.9 billion).

In the month of September alone, the overall surplus fell 30.3 percent year-on-year to 779.52 trillion yen ($6.96 trillion). The surplus with the United States in September fell 8.5 percent from a year earlier to 398.85 billion yen ($3.56 billion).
The surplus has been steadily shrinking as imports continue to grow more strongly than exports. Japan has traditionally been regarded as having an export-oriented economy.

Structural changes such as companies moving production overseas have cut exports and fuelled imports as the subsidiaries ship their finished products back to Japan. Foreign consumer products have also become popular among the Japanese, helped by the yen's surge against the dollar last year, which made imported goods cheaper.
